metas.name: ★ 8.3 · 1964 · Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
metas.description: A mentally unstable American general orders a hydrogen bomb attack on the Soviet Union, triggering a path to global nuclear holocaust that a war room full of politicians and generals frantically tries to stop.

metas.name: ★ 8.3 · 1961 · Judgment at Nuremberg
metas.description: Fictionalized depiction of the 1947 Judges' Trial, the third of 12 trials of Nazi war criminals conducted by the American occupying forces in Nuremberg, Germany, in which former judges of Nazi Germany were tried for their actions.

metas.name: ★ 8.1 · 1966 · The Battle of Algiers
metas.description: In the 1950s, fear and violence escalate as the people of Algiers fight for independence from the French government.

metas.name: ★ 8.1 · 1969 · Army of Shadows
metas.description: An account of underground resistance fighters in Nazi-occupied France.

metas.name: ★ 8.0 · 1962 · Ivan's Childhood
metas.description: During WWII, Soviet orphan Ivan Bondarev strikes up a friendship with three sympathetic Soviet officers while working as a scout behind the German lines.

metas.name: ★ 7.9 · 1965 · Doctor Zhivago
metas.description: The life of a Russian physician and poet who, although married to another, falls in love with a political activist's wife and experiences hardship during World War I and then the October Revolution.

metas.name: ★ 7.7 · 1967 · The Dirty Dozen
metas.description: During World War II, a rebellious U.S. Army Major is assigned a dozen convicted murderers to train and lead them into a mass assassination mission of German officers.

metas.name: ★ 7.7 · 1964 · Zulu
metas.description: Outnumbered British soldiers do battle with Zulu warriors at Rorke's Drift.

metas.name: ★ 7.6 · 1968 · Where Eagles Dare
metas.description: Allied agents stage a daring raid on a castle where the Nazis are holding American brigadier general George Carnaby prisoner, but that's not all that's really going on.

metas.name: ★ 7.1 · 1962 · How the West Was Won
metas.description: A family saga covering several decades of Westward expansion in the 19th century, including the Gold Rush, the Civil War, and the building of the railroads.
